title: Emergency: Rate-limit / quota / burst-policy mismatch causing multi-tenant outages
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Multiple customers (hosted API and two Dedicated tenants plus one Private deployment) reported 503 / rate-limit errors during planned traffic bursts. Initial investigation shows quota enforcement and burst-policy logic diverged after the rollout of the dynamic-burst-controller in runtime-1.27; results varied by deployment type and caused legitimate short bursts to be rejected, triggering downstream SLA breaches and a major customer escalation.
observed_behavior:
- Short legitimate bursts (2-10s) from clients were throttled and returned 429/503
- Hosted traffic showed sudden increase in throttling metrics at 2026-03-09T21:11Z
- Dedicated pool autoscaler reported capacity available but requests were blocked by quota enforcement layer
- Private deployment with local KMS saw mismatch between token-level quotas and pool-level burst windows
expected_behavior:
- Burst requests within configured burst_window and within quota should be allowed (with grace for prefix/KV cache hits)
- Quota enforcement should be consistent across hosted, dedicated, and private modes when policy equivalence is configured
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use client to fire 12 concurrent generate requests (each ~64 tokens) within a 5s window against a model route with quota=1000/min and burst_window=10s
3) Repeat against a Dedicated tenant with same config and observe differences
4) For Private, run traffic through customer VPC and confirm if local quota adapter returns inconsistent available_tokens
5) Enable runtime debug logs (rate_limit=debug) and capture controller traces for a failing request
impact_summary:
- 3 customers experienced dropped requests and increased latency; one enterprise customer escalated to a support SE and reported production outage for a user-facing feature during business hours.
- Revenue-risk: medium-high for the affected customers; on-call time consumed ~18 engineer-hours across infra/serving/SE teams.
- Operational: Console alerts and SLO pages showed elevated error budget burn for the hosted API route.
root_cause:
- A logic regression introduced in dynamic-burst-controller (PR #4412) changed the order of quota checks vs burst reconciliation. When burst reconciliation returned an adjusted token bank, the quota-enforcer performed a stale lookup against an in-memory token bucket snapshot rather than the reconciled bank under high concurrency.
- Additionally, Dedicated and Private adapters had different contract expectations for the burst_window parameter (seconds vs milliseconds), causing mismatched enforcement across deployments.
short_term_mitigation:
- Reverted dynamic-burst-controller to previous behavior on hosted lanes (rollback runtime-1.27 change) — applied hotfix 2026-03-10 23:45Z. This stopped new customers from failing immediately.
- For affected Dedicated tenants, temporarily disabled strict burst enforcement and opened a controlled grace window on their pools (config flag: pool.allow_burst_grace = true).
- For Private customer, worked with their on-prem admin to sync burst_window units and apply local patch to quota adapter.
- Communication: Notified customers via support tickets and posted incident update in #prod-incident Slack thread.
long_term_fix:
- Implement single source-of-truth for token-bank reconciliation: refactor quota-enforcer to read from reconciled bank atomically and add concurrency-safe compare-and-swap. (Planned PR: runtime/pull/4521)
- Normalize burst_window units across all adapters (hosted/dedicated/private) and add a strict schema validation for config ingestion.
- Add end-to-end tests that emulate cross-deployment burst scenarios and verify rate-limit/quota invariants.
proposed_fix:
- Code changes in runtime/service/rate_limit: replace dual-path lookup with atomic reconciler API; add unit and integration tests. Target branch: fix/atomic-burst-reconcile. Draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4521
- Config linting rule in deployment pipeline to reject mismatched burst_window units
rollout_plan:
1) Merge fix/atomic-burst-reconcile to canary channel and run smoke tests against hosted canary region (2 hours warmup).
2) If stable, promote to hosted prod in two waves (20% -> 100% over 30 minutes) with automatic rollback on >1% 5xx increase.
3) Apply Dedicated tenant config changes via tenant-release job; coordinate with Customer Success for scheduled windows.
4) For Private customers, provide patch bundle and clear upgrade instructions; optional support-assisted upgrade.
testing_plan:
- Unit tests for atomic reconciler and adapter normalization.
- Integration test harness that replays recorded real-traffic bursts from the March 9 incident.
- Load test in staging with synthetic multi-tenant bursts to validate behavior under concurrency.
- Post-deploy canary query that runs 100 burst sequences per minute and asserts <0.1% 429/503
